short: Diffusion Policies with Value-Conditional Optimization for Offline Reinforcement Learning
problem: The mechanism is described wrongly. DIVO does not condition on anything. It weights the diffusion training loss with binary advantage weights, and the diffusion model is a behavior model, not the deployed policy. The learned policy is a separate TD3+BC actor that is regularized toward diffusion samples with non-negative advantage. Family: this is a pure D4RL offline-RL paper with no robot manipulation, so it fits 'generalrl' ('Not robot-manipulation papers ... flow/diffusion policy theory') better than advbc. The 'short' field holds the full title instead of the method name.
evidence: arXiv 2511.08922 Eq. 9-10: L_PAD = E[f(s,a)·||eps − eps_omega||^2], f(s,a)=eta·1(Q_phi(s,a)−V_psi(s)). Sec. III-B: 'Within ADPO, the diffusion model serves as the behavior policy rather than the learned policy'; Eq. 12 target = pi_omega(s) if A(s,pi_omega(s))>=0; Eq. 13 actor loss −alpha·Q + beta·||pi_theta − pi_target||^2; 'Our algorithm is built upon the TD3+BC framework'. Abstract: evaluated on D4RL locomotion and AntMaze; comment field: IROS 2025.
proposed_fields: {"one_line": "DIVO (IROS 2025): trains a diffusion behavior model with binary advantage-based loss weights, then regularizes a TD3+BC actor toward diffusion samples with non-negative advantage; reports gains on D4RL locomotion and AntMaze.", "family": "generalrl", "short": "DIVO"}

The family is also a poor fit. IV-C: 'The version of RISE in our experimental evaluation has both spectral norm penalty and distance-based data augmentation'. BC is a diffusion policy trained on expert data only.

id: COST-HIL: Cost-Aware Human-in-the-Loop Reinforcement Learning for Real-World Dexterous Manipulation

problem: (1) 'No paper' is false. The repo contains paper/COST_HIL.pdf (authors Guozhong Luo et al.), and the repo description calls it a CVPR submission. The -80% is the intervention rate (percentage of training steps with human intervention, 30% to 6%), not a count of interventions. The intervention rate is the percentage of steps with human intervention during training.' PDF §5.2: 'We conduct experiments on the Zhiyuan Elf G2 robot.' PDF abstract: 'boosts the success rate from over 80% to 100% on the block grasping task, while reducing human interventions per successful attempt by more than 20%.'
